app_info.subtitle: Deploy static sites instantly
app_info.description:
One URL. Your agent ships.

Ask ChatGPT to build something for the web (a landing page, a
portfolio, a single-file demo, a generated doc) and this plugin
publishes it instantly. You get a real `*.shipstatic.com` URL you
can share immediately.

Free and anonymous: no install, no signup, no API key, with 3 days
to claim ownership and keep the site permanently. Connect a
ShipStatic account when you want the rest: custom domains, listing
everything you have published, and sites that never expire. The
plugin starts that sign-in for you.

justifications.read_only_justification: Removes a deployment and its files from the connected account.
justifications.open_world_justification: Takes a publicly reachable site offline, which changes public internet state.
justifications.destructive_justification: Permanently deletes the deployment and its files with no recovery.

justifications.read_only_justification: Returns one deployment's details and changes nothing.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads from the connected ShipStatic account and nothing beyond it; the read changes no public state.
justifications.destructive_justification: Retrieves records only; nothing is deleted, overwritten or revoked.

justifications.read_only_justification: Lists the connected account's deployments and changes nothing.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads from the connected ShipStatic account and nothing beyond it; the read changes no public state.
justifications.destructive_justification: Retrieves records only; nothing is deleted, overwritten or revoked.

justifications.read_only_justification: Replaces the labels on one of the connected account's deployments.
justifications.open_world_justification: Labels are private account metadata; the served site and its public URL are unchanged.
justifications.destructive_justification: Replaces the existing label set rather than adding to it, so a call can discard labels the user had set; the deployment and its files are untouched.

justifications.read_only_justification: Creates a new deployment from the files the user provides and publishes it at a fresh URL.
justifications.open_world_justification: Publishes content to a publicly reachable shipstatic.com URL, which is public internet state.
justifications.destructive_justification: Only adds a new deployment; it never overwrites or removes an existing one, and an anonymous deployment simply expires.

justifications.read_only_justification: Removes a custom domain from the connected account.
justifications.open_world_justification: Stops the public hostname from serving the site, which changes public internet state.

justifications.read_only_justification: Returns the DNS provider ShipStatic recorded for the domain, if known, and changes nothing.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads a stored value from the connected account's domain record; nothing is looked up on call and nothing changes.
justifications.destructive_justification: Retrieves records only; nothing is deleted, overwritten or revoked.

justifications.read_only_justification: Returns one domain's details and changes nothing.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads from the connected ShipStatic account and nothing beyond it; the read changes no public state.
justifications.destructive_justification: Retrieves records only; nothing is deleted, overwritten or revoked.

justifications.read_only_justification: Lists the connected account's domains and changes nothing.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads from the connected ShipStatic account and nothing beyond it; the read changes no public state.
justifications.destructive_justification: Retrieves records only; nothing is deleted, overwritten or revoked.

justifications.read_only_justification: Returns the DNS records to configure at the domain's DNS provider and changes nothing.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads the connected account's domain record; the DNS records it returns are configured by the user elsewhere, and the read changes nothing.
justifications.destructive_justification: Retrieves records only; nothing is deleted, overwritten or revoked.

justifications.read_only_justification: Creates a custom domain record or points an existing one at a different deployment in the connected account.
justifications.open_world_justification: Changes which site a public hostname serves once the user's DNS points at ShipStatic, which is public internet state.
justifications.destructive_justification: Re-pointing a domain replaces what that public hostname serves rather than adding to it; the previous deployment still exists and the domain can be pointed back.

justifications.read_only_justification: Returns a shareable link to the domain's DNS setup page and changes nothing.
justifications.open_world_justification: Derives a link from the connected account's domain record; nothing is created and nothing changes.
justifications.destructive_justification: Retrieves records only; nothing is deleted, overwritten or revoked.

justifications.read_only_justification: Checks whether a domain name is valid and available and changes nothing.
justifications.open_world_justification: Answers from ShipStatic's own records; nothing is reserved and nothing changes.
justifications.destructive_justification: Retrieves records only; nothing is deleted, overwritten or revoked.

justifications.read_only_justification: Queues a DNS verification for the domain, which can move it to verified and start serving the linked site.
justifications.open_world_justification: A successful verification puts the site live on the user's public hostname, which is public internet state.
justifications.destructive_justification: Only checks DNS the user configured and activates the domain; nothing is deleted or overwritten.

justifications.read_only_justification: Returns the connected account's email, name, plan, current usage and plan caps, and changes nothing.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads from the connected ShipStatic account and nothing beyond it; the read changes no public state.
justifications.destructive_justification: Retrieves account details only; nothing is deleted, overwritten or revoked.

test_cases.description: The simplest path: a single HTML page, written by the model and published with no account, no confirmation gate and no setup. The user asks for a page to be put online and shared, naming no tool and no host; the deploy card renders inline with the live URL. The screenshot tile may read "Preview loading" for up to about thirty seconds while the capture lands.
test_cases.user_prompt: Create a Paris destination page and publish it online so I can share the link.
test_cases.expected_output: A deploy card with a live *.shipstatic.com URL, "1 file" and a small byte count, a screenshot of the page, and a "Claim to keep forever" link; the reply repeats the URL. Opening it shows a one-page site about Paris as a destination.

test_cases.description: Multi-file site with cross-links. The model generates index.html, styles.css and about.html and sends all three in ONE deploy call; the stylesheet applies and the about link works on the live site.
test_cases.user_prompt: Build me a landing page for a fictional coffee shop called "Blackbird Coffee" with an index.html, a styles.css file, and a small about.html page. Deploy it.
test_cases.expected_output: A deploy card showing "3 files". The URL opens a styled landing page and its About link opens /about.html.

test_cases.description: Deterministic content the reviewer can verify with a single fetch of the URL. The model must use the exact heading and title text and must echo the deployment URL in its reply.
test_cases.user_prompt: Deploy an HTML page whose <h1> reads exactly "Hello reviewer" and whose <title> reads "ShipStatic test". Then tell me the URL.
test_cases.expected_output:
A deploy card and the URL repeated in the reply. Fetching the URL returns HTML containing exactly

Hello reviewer

and ShipStatic test.

test_cases.description: Password-protected deploy. The password option locks the published site behind a visitor unlock prompt; it is a setting for the site being published, not a credential of the reviewer's. The model passes it with the deploy and repeats it back, since a password the user never sees locks them out. The card shows a lock chip and the site asks for the password before rendering.
test_cases.user_prompt: Deploy a one-page "coming soon" landing page and protect it with the password "demo123".
test_cases.expected_output: A deploy card with a lock chip in its meta row, the password "demo123" confirmed in the reply, and a URL that prompts for the password before showing the page.

test_cases.description: The anonymous lifetime and the claim link, explained. Without an account a deployment expires in 3 days unless claimed; the tool result carries a one-time claim URL and the server's instructions tell the model to show it. The reviewer sees the model relay both facts correctly.
test_cases.user_prompt: Deploy a page that says "Keep me" and explain how I can keep this site permanently.
test_cases.expected_output: A deploy card with the live URL and the claim link, and a reply that says the site expires in 3 days unless claimed and that opening the claim link (creating a free account if needed) keeps it permanently.

negative_test_cases.description: An unrelated productivity request. Nothing about publishing a site; the plugin must not be invoked.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: What meetings do I have tomorrow?
negative_test_cases.expected_output: ChatGPT answers from its own tools or says it cannot see a calendar. ShipStatic is not called and no deploy card appears.

negative_test_cases.description: A nearby question that needs an explanation, not a deployment. The plugin's domain tools return DNS records for a domain the user owns on ShipStatic; a general question about DNS should be answered in prose without calling them.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Can you explain what a CNAME record is and how it differs from an A record?
negative_test_cases.expected_output: A plain explanation of the two record types. No ShipStatic tool is called and nothing is deployed.

negative_test_cases.description: A hosting request the plugin cannot serve. ShipStatic hosts static sites only; a server process is out of scope, so the model should say so rather than deploy something that cannot run.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Deploy my Node.js Express API server with its PostgreSQL database so it runs 24/7.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: ChatGPT explains that ShipStatic hosts static sites (HTML, CSS, JavaScript and assets) and cannot run a server or a database, and suggests what would fit instead. No deploy is attempted and no card appears.
